plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces long, drooping clusters of fragrant pea-like flowers before or as its leaves emerge. It is widely grown on pergolas, walls, and arbors in temperate gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; cultivated in Europe, Japan, and the United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine counterclockwise, and some specimens in Japan and California are over 100 years old, with one famous Sierra Madre vine covering nearly an acre.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial that carpets ancient forest floors with nodding, bell-shaped, sweetly scented flowers on arching stems that droop to one side.
plants.location: Native to Atlantic Europe, especially the United Kingdom, where about half of the world's population grows; found in deciduous woodlands
plants.funFact: Bluebells are protected under the UK Wildlife and Countryside Act, and their presence is used as an indicator of ancient woodland.

plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A small deciduous understory tree whose showy 'flowers' are actually four large petal-like bracts surrounding a cluster of tiny true yellow-green flowers. Its horizontal branching gives it an elegant layered look.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring (April to early May in the eastern United States)
plants.location: Native to eastern North America from Ontario to Florida and Mexico; widely planted as an ornamental
plants.funFact: Dogwood is the state tree of Virginia and Missouri, and its bright red fall berries are an important food source for songbirds.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.commonName: Eucalyptus-leaved? No: Southern Hemisphere Autumn Bloomer, Aloe arborescens (Krantz Aloe)
plants.description: A large, multi-stemmed succulent shrub with rosettes of toothed blue-green leaves. In late autumn to winter in the Southern Hemisphere it produces tall candle-like spikes of tubular flowers that attract sunbirds and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter in the Southern Hemisphere (starting around April to May)
plants.location: Native to southern Africa (South Africa, Malawi, Mozambique, Zimbabwe); grown in dry gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Aloe arborescens has been used traditionally as a hedge plant and for soothing burns, and its nectar-rich flowers are a vital winter food for birds in South Africa.
